blocks.text: Is sabaq mein do kaam hain. Pehla: ellipse ke saare features ek table mein ikatthe dekhna, taa ke dono shaklon (horizontal aur vertical) ka muqabla ek nazar mein ho jaye. Doosra: aise ellipse dekhna jin ka centre origin par nahi balke kisi aur point \((h, k)\) par ho. Exam ke ziyada tar sawal isi doosri qism ke hote hain, is liye examples ko dhyan se qadam ba qadam parhiye.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: Dono qism ke ellipses mein major axis lambi line segment hoti hai aur foci major axis par hote hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Table ko column ke hisaab se parhiye: doosra column bilkul pehle column jaisa hai, bas \(x\) aur \(y\) ki jagah badal gayi hai. Is liye ek column achhi tarah samajh lein, doosra khud ban jayega.
Directrix ki dono shaklein ek hi hain: \(\frac{c}{e^2} = \frac{ae}{e^2} = \frac{a}{e}\). Latera recta foci se guzarte hain, is liye un ki equations \(x = \pm ae\) (ya \(y = \pm ae\)) hain, kyunke focus \((\pm ae, 0)\) par hai.
Khud sochiye: table mein 'major axis ki equation' \(y = 0,\ -a \le x \le a\) kyun likhi hai, sirf \(y = 0\) kyun nahi? Kyunke major axis poori x-axis nahi, sirf \(A'\) se \(A\) tak ka tukra (segment) hai.

blocks.title: Sketch banane ka tareeqa
blocks.text:
Exam mein aksar 'sketch its graph' likha hota hai. Ellipse ka sketch banane ke liye graph paper par bohat saare points plot karne ki zaroorat nahi. Bas yeh paanch qadam:
Pehla: centre plot kijiye. Doosra: major axis ki direction mein centre se \(a\) faasle par dono vertices. Teesra: doosri direction mein centre se \(b\) faasle par dono co-vertices.
Chautha: in chaar kinaron ko hamwar (smooth) gol lakeer se joriye; kone nahi bante, ellipse har jagah gol hota hai. Panchwan: major axis par centre se \(c\) faasle par foci ke nuqte (dots) lagaiye, aur agar poocha jaye to directrices ko dashed lines se banaiye.
Dhyan rahe ke foci hamesha ellipse ke andar aur directrices hamesha bahar aati hain. Agar aap ke sketch mein aisa nahi to kahin hisaab mein ghalti hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Theorems se pehle ek chhota sa tajurba: ellipse \(\frac{x^2}{9} + \frac{y^2}{4} = 1\) ka vertex \((3, 0)\) hai. Ab equation mein \(x\) ki jagah \(x - 5\) aur \(y\) ki jagah \(y - 1\) rakhiye: \(\frac{(x-5)^2}{9} + \frac{(y-1)^2}{4} = 1\). Is nayi equation mein point \((8, 1)\) rakhein to \(\frac{9}{9} + 0 = 1\) aata hai. Yani purana vertex \((3, 0)\) ab \((3 + 5, 0 + 1) = (8, 1)\) par chala gaya.
Isi tarah har point 5 units right aur 1 unit upar khisak jata hai. Is ko translation (khiskana) kehte hain: shakal wohi, sirf jagah nayi. Neeche ke dono theorems isi baat ko aam (general) shakal mein likhte hain, jahan 5 ki jagah \(h\) aur 1 ki jagah \(k\) hai.
Yaad rakhiye: equation mein \(x - h\) ho to ellipse right ki taraf \(h\) units jata hai (agar \(h\) positive ho). Pehli nazar mein minus dekh kar left samajhna aam ghalti hai.
Theorem 1: (Translated forms of Ellipses)

Equation \(\frac{(x-h)^2}{a^2} + \frac{(y-k)^2}{b^2} = 1\), jahan \(a > b\), ek horizontal ellipse hai jis ke foci \(F'(h - c, k)\) aur \(F(h + c, k)\) hain, aur \(c = \sqrt{a^2 - b^2}\). Is ka centre point \(C(h, k)\) hai, vertices major axis par \((h \pm a, k)\) hain, aur co-vertices \((h, k \pm b)\) hain.

blocks.alt: Pale yellow panel par cyan horizontal ellipse, centre C(h, k) magenta major aur minor axis par. Vertices: baayen (bina label) aur A(h + a, k); foci F'(h - c, k) aur F(h + c, k); co-vertices B(h, k + b) upar aur B'(h, k - b) neeche; aadhe axes par a aur b likha hai. Dono taraf cyan khari directrices x = h - a^2/c aur x = h + a^2/c.
blocks.caption: Figure 6.16: horizontal ellipse with centre (h, k) (the book uses the number 6.16 twice; original drawing after the textbook's Figure 6.16)

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ki Figure 6.16 (safha 192) mein right wale focus par \(F'(h + c, k)\) likha hai, jab ke woh \(F(h + c, k)\) hai. Centre ko \(C'(h.k)\) aur upar wale co-vertex ko \(B(h.k + b)\) likha hai, comma ki jagah dot ke saath; sahi \(C(h, k)\) aur \(B(h, k + b)\) hain. Right wale vertex par \(B(h + a, k)\) likha hai; woh asal mein vertex \(A(h + a, k)\) hai. Figure number 6.16 bhi do dafa istemal hua hai (6.4.1 wali figure ka bhi yahi number hai). Humari drawing mein sahi labels hain.
Theorem 2:

Equation \(\frac{(x-h)^2}{b^2} + \frac{(y-k)^2}{a^2} = 1\), jahan \(a > b\), ek vertical ellipse hai jis ke foci \(F'(h, k - c)\) aur \(F(h, k + c)\) hain, aur \(c = \sqrt{a^2 - b^2}\). Is ka centre \(C(h, k)\) hai, vertices major axis par \((h, k \pm a)\) hain, aur co-vertices \((h \pm b, k)\) hain.

blocks.alt: Pale yellow panel par cyan vertical ellipse, centre C(h, k) magenta major (khari) aur minor (leti) axis par. Vertices A(h, k + a) upar aur A'(h, k - a) neeche, major axis par do foci dots se; co-vertices B'(h - b, k) aur B(h + b, k); a aur b likha hai. Upar neeche magenta directrices y = k + a^2/c aur y = k - a^2/c.
blocks.caption: Figure 6.17: vertical ellipse with centre (h, k) (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 6.17)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
\((x - h)\) ellipse ko khiskata kyun hai? Equation \(\frac{(x-h)^2}{a^2} + \frac{(y-k)^2}{b^2} = 1\) mein point \((h, k)\) bilkul wohi kaam kar raha hai jo pehle \((0, 0)\) kar raha tha. Purane ellipse ka har point \(h\) units right aur \(k\) units upar chala gaya. Shakal, \(a\), \(b\), \(c\) aur \(e\) nahi badalte; sirf jagah badalti hai. Bilkul aise jaise aap ek tasveer ko deewar par ek keel se utha kar doosri keel par taang dein: tasveer wohi, jagah nayi.
Rule: pehle har feature aise nikaliye jaise centre origin par ho, phir x-coordinate mein \(h\) aur y-coordinate mein \(k\) jama kar dijiye.
Signs ka dhyan: \((x + 3)^2\) ka matlab \(h = -3\) hai, kyunke \(x + 3 = x - (-3)\). Isi tarah \((y - 2)^2\) ka matlab \(k = +2\).

Ab examples ki taraf chalte hain. Example 18 mein humein ellipse ki equation di nahi gayi, balke us ke kuch hisse (foci aur major axis ki lambai) diye gaye hain, aur equation banani hai. Aise sawal mein hamesha chaar cheezein dhoondiye: centre kahan hai, major axis kis direction mein hai, \(a\) kitna hai, aur \(b\) kitna hai. Jaise hi yeh chaar mil jayein, equation seedhi likhi ja sakti hai. Foci ka x-coordinate ek jaisa ho to major axis khari (vertical) hogi, aur y-coordinate ek jaisa ho to leti hui (horizontal).

blocks.title: Example 18
blocks.problem: Find an equation of the ellipse with foci (2, 1), (2, 7), major axis of length 10 and sketch its graph.
steps:
Diya gaya: foci (2, 1) aur (2, 7); major axis ki lambai 10.
Maloom karna: ellipse ki equation aur us ka sketch.
Tareeqa: foci se major axis ki direction aur centre milenge; lambai se \(a\); centre se focus tak faasle se \(c\); phir \(b^2 = a^2 - c^2\); aur aakhir mein Theorem 2 se equation. Yeh tareeqa isliye theek hai ke ellipse ki equation likhne ke liye bas centre, direction, \(a\) aur \(b\) chahiye.

Major axis ki direction
Dono foci ka x-coordinate 2 hai, yani dono vertical line \(x = 2\) par hain.
\[\Rightarrow \text{Major axis vertical hai}\]
Kyun: foci hamesha major axis par hote hain. Jis line par foci hain, wohi major axis ki line hai.

\(a\) nikalein
\[\text{Major axis ki lambai} = 10\]
\[2a = 10 \Rightarrow a = 5\]
Kyun: major axis ki lambai \(2a\) hoti hai (vertex se vertex).

Centre nikalein
\[\text{Centre} = \left(\frac{2+2}{2}, \frac{1+7}{2}\right)\]
\[= (2, 4)\]
Kyun: centre dono foci ke bilkul beech mein hota hai, is liye midpoint formula lagaya.

\(c\) nikalein
\[c = |4 - 1| = 3\]
Kyun: \(c\) centre se kisi bhi focus tak ka faasla hai. Dono points ek hi vertical line par hain, is liye sirf y-coordinates ka farq kaafi hai.

\(b\) nikalein
\[c^2 = a^2 - b^2\]
\[9 = 25 - b^2\]
\[b^2 = 16 \Rightarrow b = 4\]
Kyun: har ellipse mein \(a\), \(b\), \(c\) ka yahi rishta hai.
Dhyan dein: \(b^2 = a^2 + c^2\) mat likhiye; ellipse mein minus hai.

Equation likhein
Centre \((h, k) = (2, 4)\), major axis vertical, \(a = 5\), \(b = 4\):
\[\frac{(x-h)^2}{b^2} + \frac{(y-k)^2}{a^2} = 1\]
\[\frac{(x-2)^2}{16} + \frac{(y-4)^2}{25} = 1\]
Kyun: vertical major axis mein bara number \(a^2\) \(y\) wale term ke neeche jata hai (Theorem 2).

Sketch
Vertices \((2, 4 \pm 5)\): \(A(2, 9)\) aur \(A'(2, -1)\).
Co-vertices \((2 \pm 4, 4)\): \(B(6, 4)\) aur \(B'(-2, 4)\).
In chaar kinaron, centre aur foci ko plot kar ke hamwar (smooth) oval banaiye (Figure 6.18).
Kyun: chaar kinare aur centre mil kar ellipse ko poori tarah tay kar dete hain.

Tasdeeq:
\(A(2, 9)\) rakhein: \(\frac{0}{16} + \frac{25}{25} = 1\). \(A\) se foci tak faasle \(9 - 7 = 2\) aur \(9 - 1 = 8\), jama \(10 = 2a\). Definition bhi poori ho gayi.

blocks.alt: Example 18 ki exact graph, pale yellow panel par: magenta axes, x-axis par -4 se 9 aur y-axis par -2 se 10 tak numbered ticks. Cyan ellipse (x - 2)^2/16 + (y - 4)^2/25 = 1; magenta major axis A'(2, -1) se A(2, 9) tak aur minor axis B'(-2, 4) se B(6, 4) tak; centre C(2, 4), foci F(2, 7) aur F'(2, 1).
blocks.caption: Figure 6.18: the ellipse of Example 18 (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 6.18)

blocks.title: Is example se kya seekha
blocks.text:
Example 18 mein humne ek nizaam (system) se kaam kiya: direction, \(a\), centre, \(c\), \(b\), aur phir equation. Har qadam pichle qadam par khara tha. Yahi tarteeb aap ke exam ke har 'equation find karo' wale sawal mein kaam aayegi.
Tasdeeq ka tareeqa bhi yaad rakhiye: koi vertex equation mein rakh kar dekhiye ke 1 aata hai ya nahi, aur ellipse ki definition (foci se faaslon ka jama \(2a\)) bhi check kar lijiye. Do minute ki tasdeeq poore sawal ke number bacha leti hai.

Example 19 mein centre origin par hai, aur humein sirf ek focus aur ek vertex diya gaya hai. Yahan symmetry humari madad karti hai: ellipse centre ke gird dono taraf bilkul barabar hota hai, is liye agar ek focus right par hai to doosra usi faasle par left par hoga. Isi tarah vertex ka bhi.

blocks.title: Example 19
blocks.problem: Find an equation of the ellipse with centre (0, 0), focus (5, 0) and vertex (6, 0). Sketch its graph.
steps:
Diya gaya: centre (0, 0), focus (5, 0), vertex (6, 0).
Maloom karna: equation aur sketch.
Tareeqa: symmetry se doosra focus aur doosra vertex, phir \(a\) aur \(c\), phir \(b^2 = a^2 - c^2\).

Doosra focus aur vertex
Focus \((5, 0)\) right par hai, to symmetry se doosra focus \((-5, 0)\).
Vertex \((6, 0)\) right par hai, to doosra vertex \((-6, 0)\).
Kyun: ellipse apne centre ke gird symmetric hai; har point ka 'aaina' doosri taraf bhi hota hai.

Major axis ki direction
Saare points ka y-coordinate 0 hai, is liye major axis horizontal hai (x-axis par).
Kyun: foci aur vertices major axis par hote hain.

\(a\) aur \(c\)
\[(\pm 6, 0) \Rightarrow a = 6,\ a^2 = 36\]
\[(\pm 5, 0) \Rightarrow c = 5,\ c^2 = 25\]
Kyun: \(a\) centre se vertex tak, \(c\) centre se focus tak ka faasla hai.

\(b\) nikalein
\[c^2 = a^2 - b^2\]
\[25 = 36 - b^2\]
\[b^2 = 11 \Rightarrow b = \sqrt{11}\]
Kyun: ellipse ka rishta. \(\sqrt{11}\) ko waise hi rehne dein, decimal mein badalne ki zaroorat nahi.

Equation likhein
\[\frac{x^2}{a^2} + \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1\]
\[\frac{x^2}{36} + \frac{y^2}{11} = 1\]
Kyun: major axis horizontal hai, is liye \(a^2 = 36\) \(x^2\) ke neeche.

Sketch
Vertices \((\pm 6, 0)\), co-vertices \((0, \pm\sqrt{11}) \approx (0, \pm 3.3)\), foci \((\pm 5, 0)\) (Figure 6.19).
Kyun: yeh points curve ko tay karte hain.

Tasdeeq:
\(a^2 - b^2 = 36 - 11 = 25 = c^2\), to foci \((\pm 5, 0)\) hi aate hain, aur \((6, 0)\) rakhne se \(\frac{36}{36} + 0 = 1\).

blocks.alt: Example 19 ki exact graph, pale yellow panel par: magenta axes, x-axis par -10 ka tick aur y-axis par 5 aur -5 ke ticks. Cyan ellipse x^2/36 + y^2/11 = 1: centre O(0, 0), vertices A'(-6, 0) aur A(6, 0), foci F'(-5, 0) aur F(5, 0), co-vertices B(0, root 11) aur B'(0, -root 11).
blocks.caption: Figure 6.19: the ellipse of Example 19 (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 6.19)

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ki Figure 6.19 mein dono foci par prime laga hai: \(F'(-5, 0)\) aur \(F'(5, 0)\). Right wala focus \(F(5, 0)\) hai. Humari drawing mein sahi label hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Example 19 mein agar vertex \((6, 0)\) ki jagah \((0, 6)\) diya hota, aur focus \((0, 5)\), to kya badalta? Saare points y-axis par hote, is liye major axis vertical hoti aur equation \(\frac{x^2}{11} + \frac{y^2}{36} = 1\) banti. Numbers wohi, sirf jagah badal gayi.
Aur agar focus \((5, 0)\) aur vertex \((0, 6)\) diye hote? Yeh mumkin hi nahi, kyunke focus aur vertex dono major axis par hone chahiye. Aisa data dekh kar foran samajh jaiye ke sawal mein kuch ghalat hai.
Is tarah ke 'agar aisa hota to' wale sawal khud se poochiye; yeh concept ko pakka karne ka sab se tez tareeqa hai, aur exam mein ghalti pakarne ki aadat bhi daalta hai.

Example 20 is sabaq ka sab se ahem example hai, kyunke yahan equation general shakal mein di gayi hai: \(16x^2 + 9y^2 - 64x + 54y + 1 = 0\). Is shakal mein na centre nazar aata hai na \(a\), \(b\). Hamara kaam is equation ko 'saaf' kar ke translated standard form mein lana hai, jis ke liye complete the square ka tareeqa use hoga. Yeh tareeqa aap ne circle (6.1) mein bhi dekha tha; yahan farq sirf itna hai ke \(x^2\) aur \(y^2\) ke coefficients alag alag (16 aur 9) hain, is liye har bracket ka coefficient alag se bahar nikalna parta hai.

blocks.title: Example 20
blocks.problem: Find the centre, foci, eccentricity, vertices and directrices of the ellipse whose equation is \(16x^2 + 9y^2 - 64x + 54y + 1 = 0\). Also sketch its graph.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(16x^2 + 9y^2 - 64x + 54y + 1 = 0\).
Maloom karna: centre, foci, eccentricity, vertices, directrices aur sketch.
Tareeqa: yeh general shakal hai, is mein se kuch seedha nazar nahi aata. Is liye \(x\) aur \(y\) dono mein complete the square kar ke translated standard form banayenge, phir Theorem 2 se muqabla karenge.

Terms ko group karein aur coefficients bahar nikalein
\[16x^2 + 9y^2 - 64x + 54y + 1 = 0\]
\[(16x^2 - 64x) + (9y^2 + 54y) + 1 = 0\]
\[16(x^2 - 4x) + 9(y^2 + 6y) + 1 = 0\]
Kyun: complete the square ke liye bracket ke andar \(x^2\) aur \(y^2\) ka coefficient 1 hona chahiye.

Squares complete karein
\[16[(x^2 - 4x + 4) - 4]\]
\[\quad + 9[(y^2 + 6y + 9) - 9] + 1 = 0\]
\[16[(x-2)^2 - 4] + 9[(y+3)^2 - 9] + 1 = 0\]
\[16(x-2)^2 - 64 + 9(y+3)^2 - 81 + 1 = 0\]
\[16(x-2)^2 + 9(y+3)^2 - 144 = 0\]
\[16(x-2)^2 + 9(y+3)^2 = 144\]
Kyun: \(-4\) ka aadha \(-2\), aur \((-2)^2 = 4\); \(6\) ka aadha \(3\), aur \(3^2 = 9\). Ek hi number jama aur minus karne se equation nahi badalti.
Dhyan dein: bracket ke bahar 16 hai, is liye andar ka \(-4\) bahar aa kar \(-64\) banta hai, aur \(-9\) ko 9 se zarb de kar \(-81\).

Dono sides ko 144 se divide karein
\[\frac{16(x-2)^2}{144} + \frac{9(y+3)^2}{144} = 1\]
\[\frac{(x-2)^2}{9} + \frac{(y+3)^2}{16} = 1\]
Kyun: standard form mein right side par 1 hota hai.

Standard form se muqabla
\(\frac{(x-h)^2}{b^2} + \frac{(y-k)^2}{a^2} = 1\) se muqabla karne par:
\[h = 2,\ k = -3,\ b^2 = 9 \Rightarrow b = 3\]
\[a^2 = 16 \Rightarrow a = 4\]
\(a > b\) aur \(a^2\) \(y\) wale term ke neeche hai, is liye major axis vertical hai. Centre: \(C(2, -3)\).
Kyun: bara denominator hamesha \(a^2\) hai, aur \(y + 3 = y - (-3)\) se \(k = -3\).

\(c\) aur \(e\)
\[c^2 = a^2 - b^2 = 16 - 9 = 7\]
\[c = \sqrt{7}\]
\[e = \frac{c}{a} = \frac{\sqrt{7}}{4}\]
Kyun: ellipse ka rishta aur eccentricity ki definition. \(e < 1\) aaya, jo ellipse ke liye zaroori hai.

Vertices
Vertices centre se \(a = 4\) units upar aur neeche, vertical axis par:
\[A(2, -3 + 4) = A(2, 1)\]
\[A'(2, -3 - 4) = A'(2, -7)\]
Kyun: vertices major axis par centre se \(a\) faasle par hote hain; x-coordinate wohi rehta hai.

Foci
Foci centre se \(c = \sqrt{7}\) units upar aur neeche:
\[F(2, -3 + \sqrt{7})\]
\[F'(2, -3 - \sqrt{7})\]
Kyun: foci bhi major axis par hain, centre se \(c\) faasle par.

Directrices
Vertical major axis ke liye directrices horizontal lines \(y = k \pm \frac{a}{e}\) hain:
\[y = -3 \pm \frac{4}{\sqrt{7}/4}\]
\[y = -3 \pm \frac{16}{\sqrt{7}}\]
Kyun: directrix major axis par perpendicular hoti hai aur centre se \(\frac{a}{e}\) faasle par.
Dhyan dein: \(k = -3\) jama karna mat bhooliye.

Sketch
\(C(2, -3)\), \(A(2, 1)\), \(A'(2, -7)\), co-vertices \((2 \pm 3, -3)\) yani \(B'(-1, -3)\) aur \((5, -3)\), aur foci plot kar ke hamwar oval banaiye (Figure 6.20).
Kyun: yeh points curve ko tay karte hain.

Tasdeeq:
Vertex \((2, 1)\) asal equation mein rakhein: \(16(4) + 9(1) - 64(2) + 54(1) + 1 = 64 + 9 - 128 + 54 + 1 = 0\). Sahi.

blocks.alt: Example 20 ki exact graph, pale yellow panel par: magenta axes, x-axis par -5 aur 5, y-axis par -5. Cyan ellipse (x - 2)^2/9 + (y + 3)^2/16 = 1; magenta major axis A'(2, -7) se A(2, 1) tak, minor axis B'(-1, -3) se (5, -3) tak; centre C(2, -3); foci F(2, -3 + root 7) (x-axis ke bilkul neeche) aur F'(2, -3 - root 7).
blocks.caption: Figure 6.20: the ellipse of Example 20 (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 6.20)

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ki Figure 6.20 mein label \(F(2, -3 + \sqrt{7})\) point \((5, -3)\) ke saath chhapa hai, jo minor axis ka daayan sira hai. Focus \(F(2, -3 + \sqrt{7}) \approx (2, -0.35)\) major axis (khari line \(x = 2\)) par hai, \(x\)-axis ke bilkul neeche. Hamari drawing mein label focus par hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Sketch ke liye andaze ki qeematein madad karti hain: \(\sqrt{7} \approx 2.65\), to foci taqreeban \((2, -0.35)\) aur \((2, -5.65)\) par, aur directrices taqreeban \(y \approx 3.05\) aur \(y \approx -9.05\) par, yani ellipse ke bahar, jaisa hona chahiye.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Example 20 mein agar \(x^2\) ka coefficient 9 aur \(y^2\) ka 16 hota, yani \(9x^2 + 16y^2 + \ldots = 0\), to kya major axis phir bhi vertical hoti? (Nahi. Divide karne ke baad bara denominator \(x\) wale term ke neeche aata, aur major axis horizontal hoti.)
Yaad rakhiye: jis variable ke saath chhota coefficient ho, divide karne ke baad usi ke neeche bara denominator aata hai, aur major axis usi direction mein hoti hai. Yeh chhota sa jaanch ka tareeqa (shortcut) aap ko sawal shuru karte hi direction bata deta hai.
Ek aur sawal: agar complete the square ke baad right side negative aa jaye, maslan \(16(x-2)^2 + 9(y+3)^2 = -5\), to kya hoga? (Do squares ka jama negative nahi ho sakta, is liye koi point nahi milega; aisi equation koi real ellipse nahi deti.)

Example 21 mein saari maloomat lafzon mein di gayi hai. Is qism ke sawal mein pehla kaam yeh hai ke har jumle ko math ki zabaan mein badlein: 'major axis ki lambai 10' ka matlab \(2a = 10\), 'foci ke darmiyan faasla 6' ka matlab \(2c = 6\). Aksar bachche \(c = 6\) likh dete hain, jab ke 6 dono foci ka faasla hai, centre se ek focus ka nahi.

blocks.title: Example 21
blocks.problem:
An ellipse has the following properties:
(i) Its major axis is vertical and has a length of 10 units.
(ii) The distance between its foci is 6 units.
(iii) The centre of the ellipse is at the point (3, -2).
Find the standard equation of this ellipse.
steps:
Diya gaya: major axis vertical, lambai 10; foci ke darmiyan faasla 6; centre (3, -2).
Maloom karna: standard equation.
Tareeqa: lambaiyon se \(a\) aur \(c\), phir \(b^2 = a^2 - c^2\), phir Theorem 2. Centre aur direction pehle se diye hue hain, is liye kaam aasaan hai.

(i) Major axis
\[2a = 10 \Rightarrow a = 5 \Rightarrow a^2 = 25\]
Kyun: major axis ki lambai \(2a\) hai.

(ii) Foci ka faasla
\[2c = 6 \Rightarrow c = 3 \Rightarrow c^2 = 9\]
Kyun: centre ke dono taraf \(c\) faasle par ek ek focus hai, to dono ke darmiyan \(2c\).

(iii) Centre
\[(h, k) = (3, -2)\]
Kyun: sawal mein diya hua hai.

Equation likhein
Major axis vertical hai, is liye form \(\frac{(x-h)^2}{b^2} + \frac{(y-k)^2}{a^2} = 1\). \(h = 3\), \(k = -2\), \(a^2 = 25\), \(b^2 = 16\) rakhein:
\[\frac{(x-3)^2}{16} + \frac{(y+2)^2}{25} = 1\]
Kyun: vertical major axis, to \(a^2\) \(y\) wale term ke neeche; aur \(y - (-2) = y + 2\).
Dhyan dein: \((y - 2)\) likhna sab se aam ghalti hai.

Tasdeeq:
Foci \((3, -2 \pm 3)\), yani \((3, 1)\) aur \((3, -5)\), ka faasla 6 hai, aur vertices \((3, 3)\), \((3, -7)\) ka faasla 10. Dono shartein poori.

blocks.title: Is sabaq ka khulasa
blocks.text:
Charon examples ko saath rakh kar dekhiye. Example 18, 19 aur 21 mein data se equation banayi; Example 20 mein equation se data nikala. Yani ellipse ke sawal do hi qism ke hain: 'data se equation' ya 'equation se data'.
Pehli qism mein: centre, direction, \(a\), \(c\), phir \(b\), phir equation. Doosri qism mein: complete the square, right side 1, phir muqabla kar ke \(h\), \(k\), \(a\), \(b\), aur un se \(c\), \(e\), vertices, foci, directrices.
Dono qismon mein ek hi rishta \(c^2 = a^2 - b^2\) bunyaad (foundation) hai. Is ko achhi tarah yaad kar lijiye, kyunke Exercise 6.4 ka taqreeban har sawal isi par chalta hai.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text:
Board ke paper mein is section se aam taur par do qism ke sawal aate hain: diye gaye data se ellipse ki equation, ya general equation se centre, foci, eccentricity, vertices aur directrices. Dono mein jawab ke saath har qadam likhiye, kyunke marks qadmon par milte hain, sirf aakhri jawab par nahi.
Directrices likhte waqt hamesha poori line ki equation likhiye, maslan \(y = -3 \pm \frac{16}{\sqrt{7}}\), sirf number nahi.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Ellipse \(\frac{(x+1)^2}{25} + \frac{(y-2)^2}{9} = 1\) ke features: bara denominator 25, \(x\) wale term ke neeche, to horizontal. Centre \((-1, 2)\), \(a = 5\), \(b = 3\), \(c = 4\).
Pehle origin wale ellipse ke features: vertices \((\pm 5, 0)\), foci \((\pm 4, 0)\). Ab centre jama karein: vertices \((-1 \pm 5, 2)\) yani \((4, 2)\) aur \((-6, 2)\); foci \((3, 2)\) aur \((-5, 2)\).
\(e = \frac{4}{5}\), directrices \(x = -1 \pm \frac{25}{4}\).
Khud sochiye: is ellipse ke co-vertices kya honge? (Jawab: \((-1, 5)\) aur \((-1, -1)\).)

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
Horizontal: \(\frac{(x-h)^2}{a^2} + \frac{(y-k)^2}{b^2} = 1\); foci \((h \pm c, k)\), vertices \((h \pm a, k)\), co-vertices \((h, k \pm b)\), directrices \(x = h \pm \frac{a}{e}\).
Vertical: \(\frac{(x-h)^2}{b^2} + \frac{(y-k)^2}{a^2} = 1\); foci \((h, k \pm c)\), vertices \((h, k \pm a)\), co-vertices \((h \pm b, k)\), directrices \(y = k \pm \frac{a}{e}\).
General equation di ho to: complete the square, right side 1 banaiye, phir \(h\), \(k\), \(a\), \(b\) parhiye.
Data diya ho to: centre, major axis ki direction, \(a\) aur \(c\) nikaliye; phir \(b^2 = a^2 - c^2\).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
Centre jama karna bhool jana: centre \((2, -3)\) ho to foci \((2, -3 \pm \sqrt{7})\) hain, \((0, \pm\sqrt{7})\) nahi.
Translated ellipse ki directrices \(y = \pm\frac{a}{e}\) likh dena; sahi \(y = k \pm \frac{a}{e}\) hai.
Coefficient bahar ho to complete the square mein sirf 4 minus karna, jab ke \(16 \times 4 = 64\) minus hona chahiye.
\((x + 3)\) dekh kar \(h = 3\) likh dena; sahi \(h = -3\) hai.
